2772.headline: Where this game is in its run

2773.body:
"Sugar Skull Cash" has 277,671 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $1,000 prize, with 37 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything here about "Sugar Skull Cash" comes from official Texas lottery numbers, current through November 21.
2773.headline: What's actually left to win

2774.body:
"The Price is Right™" offers a top prize of $250,000 and eleven prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay out often, in small amounts. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

Everything here about "The Price is Right™" comes from official Texas lottery numbers, current through November 21.
2774.headline: How the prize money is divided

2775.body:
"Casino 7s" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $100,000 was claimed earlier this week. Unsold tickets still hold three of the original four. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

The numbers for "Casino 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2775.headline: Another top prize was claimed

2776.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "Patriotic Payout" have been sold. The game is early in its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

The numbers for "Patriotic Payout" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2776.headline: How far along this game is

2779.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "Gnome for the Holidays" have been sold. The game is near the start of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, top prizes are going faster than tickets, which is not a good sign.

Everything here about "Gnome for the Holidays" comes from official Texas lottery numbers, current through November 21.
2779.headline: How far along this game is

2780.body:
"Holiday Countdown" is near the start of its run, with about three-quarters of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "Holiday Countdown" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2780.headline: How much has sold

2781.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "The Perfect Gift" are sold. The top prize count has held, with five of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Every line of The Perfect Gift's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2781.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

2782.body:
The top prize count on "$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has four of four top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
2782.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

2783.body:
"30X The Cash" is new from the Texas Lottery. It is a $2 game with five top prizes of $30,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

Everything here about "30X The Cash" comes from official Texas lottery numbers, current through November 21.
2783.headline: A new game is here

2784.body:
"Lucky Scratch" just reached Texas stores with four top prizes of $100,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the overall odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

Every line of Lucky Scratch's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2784.headline: New in stores
